## Complete signed assembly and new integral helpers

Lines 55–58 state `hIntegralAdd` with explicit functions and genuine `Integrable` hypotheses for both summands. Its conclusion is exactly pointwise addition inside the integral; its proof is the pinned `integral_add`. The helper's domain `{A : Type}` is sufficient for every use: finite real paths or the product of such a path and a finite label permutation. It does not constrain the public Brownian sample universe, because no helper use integrates over that arbitrary sample space. The original arbitrary `ΩB` only supplies the bridge law `Q`. The actual final public universe TYPE remains an outstanding machine audit requirement.

Lines 99–402 were read as one complete `hPositive`-to-public-conclusion assembly, including all source-kernel measurability, L1, nonnegativity and constants. `hData` uses the actual halfline/interval derivative data under the actual Brownian bridge and the accepted interval regularity. `source_parts_measurable_integrable` supplies genuine L1 for the signed bill and each halfline summand. Measurable indicators of the weak-bad and prior-hit events preserve L1; the proof does not obtain a finite numerical bound by allowing a nonintegrable Bochner integral to default to zero.

The two alive-complement facts, lines 241–256, explicitly convert the dependent existential resulting from negating the prefix quantifier to the conjunction existential in `oppositePrefixHit`. They cover the same ranks `k ≤ r`; lower alive failure pays the upper halfline, and upper alive failure pays the lower halfline. The lower sign reversal and `neg_le_neg_iff` preserve the closed hit endpoint. No atom or equality case disappears.

The entire rank classification, lines 257–313, uses the accepted actual classification. Its strict bad test is enlarged to the closed weak-bad test. In the added equality case the upper/lower halfline terms and the negative interval positive part are nonnegative, so the enlargement is valid. The two prior indicators are the exact complements above, not replacements based on an assumption about the cap. The actual interval overshoot is retained with a negative sign in the signed source, with its negative part supplied by the accepted C12 budget.

The complete finite-sum assembly, lines 318–336, now provides each Nat-indexed function explicitly to Fin/range conversion: the signed bill, the paired ordinary terms, the weak-bad paired terms, and the negative interval positive part. The functions use the same actual rank, cap and permutation. The prior sum is already over `Fin n`. Distributing sums and factoring the constant yields exactly `CK exp(-x²) ordinary + bad + negative + prior`, without an extra copy or lost term.

The new explicit outer integral rewrites, lines 384–390, have L1 hypotheses for all four complete summands, with the coefficient `CK exp(-x²)` consistently included. They preserve the nesting of additions in the integrand. The Gaussian conversion, reviewed in its complete surrounding proof, pays `exp(-x²) ≤ 3 Psi(x)` for `x ≥ 16`. The final law-independent constant remains `3 CK CO + CP + CB + CN`.

Lines 1253–1265 prove `hPairedIntegral` for an arbitrary finite subset of `Fin n` and two full path functions. Each paired term is integrable by addition; `integral_finsetSum` applies with its full membership hypotheses, `hIntegralAdd` applies separately to every rank, and `sum_add_distrib` separates the two actual sums. Its uses with all ranks, `earlySet`, and `lateSet` supply exactly the corresponding upper/lower envelope L1 proofs. This helper does not assume the conclusion of any payment.

## Log ratio, true product disintegration and signed prefix law

The complete `hLogRatio`, lines 404–428, was checked independently. For `0 < u ≤ v`, tangent log gives `log(1+v)-log(1+u) ≤ (v-u)/(1+u)` and the lower log bound gives `u/(1+u) ≤ log(1+u)`. Multiplication uses only nonnegative `u` and `v-u`. The new `linarith only` additions avoid the previously wrong orientation of an additive monotonicity lemma. Cross multiplication uses strictly positive `v,u`. The resulting ratio inequality and the unchanged complete early endpoint proof have identical mathematical content to source02. In particular gamma remains `1/160000`, the legal endpoint remains `A=x sqrt(n)/2`, and the direct bound remains `Rj ≤ (j/n) exp(-2x²)`; no weaker endpoint or summation hypothesis has been substituted.

The complete path splitting and distribution transfer at lines 717–770 were read. Head energy and true suffix energy/sum use actual head/tail identities and permutation invariance of the full finite sum. `randomReorder` has pushforward exactly the unmasked iid product law. No cap, energy event or bad event is retained in a claimed independent distribution.

The complete suffix profile identification at 771–809 keeps the actual suffix length `n-j`. `hBadFuture` first splits the length gate `m ≤ n-j`; when false the whole original conjunction is false, and when true the remaining original energy and closed threshold predicates are unchanged. This fixes contradictory tactical branches without changing the event or profile. In particular the threshold is exactly `sqrt(9x²/4−1) sqrt(suffixEnergy)` and not the rank-r weak-bad event used before deleting the crossing label.

The entire `hSignedDI` proof, lines 857–878, was read with its support transfer and record increment definition. The explicit `change` exposes the actual norm of the composed `D`. Bounded coordinates and `|s|=1` give `|prefixSum(s·v)| ≤ j Bcap`; the previous maximum is nonnegative, so `0 ≤ D(s·v) ≤ j Bcap`, also for `j=0`. This is a genuine L1 dominator under the probability law.

The complete disintegration lemma `hBlock`, lines 881–923, is valid for every measurable suffix-dependent prefix amplitude dominated by this signed `D`, and every nonnegative integrable future profile. The split map sends the full n-fold iid measure to `law j × law(n-j)`. The product `D(s·head) V(tail)` is integrable, dominates the absolute value of the amplitude product, and justifies the Fubini exchange. The inner integral is evaluated at the actual nonnegative suffix energy. The bound `K` is applied pointwise only to that suffix energy and then integrated against the nonnegative `V`. It makes no claim that the energy-floor indicator, actual wall, cap, or weak-bad event is independent of the prefix or suffix.

Lines 925–966 transfer only the prefix law to `eta(s)=map(z ↦ s z) rho`. Support, mean, variance, beta, and energy are verified for `s=±1`. The scalar coordinate map is now explicitly measurable in `hSignMap`; the actual `pi_map_pi` has finite index type and sigma-finite mapped coordinate measures. Those measures are probability measures (measurable pushforwards of rho), so its hypotheses are available. `hSignIntegral` is an actual map-integral equality. The suffix law in all envelopes remains the original rho product. No symmetry of rho is assumed.

The complete prefix ordinary/early bounds and actual record identifications through line 1139 were read, not only the explicit-argument rewrites. Nonempty floored strips force `j ≥ x² ≥ 256`; the small `j<12` branch is empty, so accepted producer guards hold. The closed strip and endpoint events are unchanged. `hDRecord` now passes the actual head length `r+1`, its length guard and the reflexive prefix bound explicitly. `hActualStrip` reduces membership before using head/tail energy addition and sign energy invariance. On total energy at least `n/2`, the floor equals the original actual wall. The ordinary envelope domination then drops the high-energy mask pointwise and integrates the unmasked envelope.

## Ordinary and early payments, with all finite indices

The full block from 1140–1335 was read. Each actual rank is `r ∈ Fin n`, each prefix length `j=r.val+1`, and true suffix length `t=n-(r.val+1)`. The last rank therefore has t=0. The W producer supplies both its pointwise nonnegativity/L1 and exact zero at t=0. The early denominator comparison uses `t+beta² ≥ n/2`, giving the required `2 CW/sqrt(n)` bound.

`hWReindex` uses the actual permutation `Fin.revPerm`, whose function is `Fin.rev`. Its actual core value is definitionally `n-(r.val+1)`, exactly the suffix length. Exposing the composed dependent integral in the `change` keeps the path dimension equal to this value. It rearranges the full rank set once and converts to `range n`, which contains t=0 through n−1, not n and not a shifted range. Enlarging to `Icc 0 n` uses nonnegativity and the accepted grid bound, so it cannot create an omitted singular endpoint.

`hEnvSum` now separates the constant sum before factoring the weighted sum. There are exactly n copies of the early majorant, and the other term uses coefficient `160000 CU beta/n ≥ 0`. The equality at 1241–1252 is checked algebraically in its complete form: n cancels only against positive n, and `beta/n * sqrt(n)=delta` follows from positive sqrt(n) and its square n. This yields `2 CE CW delta exp(-2x²)+160000 CU CW delta` per wall.

The ordinary integral uses the full paired helper under P and the exact randomReorder transfer. Its factor 6 and two walls give `CEarly=24 CE CW` and `1920000 CU CW`. L1 is established separately for GOrd, its reveal-law pullback, high, low, and ordinary. The low/high split is exhaustive at energy=n/2, assigned to high. The ordinary constant remains `CO=CL+CEarly+1920000 CU CW+1` and is independent of the law.

The complete early-set L1, pointwise domination and payment, lines 1396–1490, also use the full paired summand and at most n early ranks. No real-power rank sum is introduced. The arbitrary cap remains present only in the actual O terms and is dropped by the pointwise envelope. `base=low+earlyHigh` pays `(CL+CEarly) delta exp(-2x²)`.

## Arbitrary cap tail and full-rank prior-hit payment

The complete tail block at 1336–1395 was read. `tailNu` uses every rank at or after tau. For r<kappa, actual halfline cap monotonicity compares the arbitrary nu to kappa using only nu≤kappa and nonnegative actual halfline integrands. For r≥kappa, nu≤kappa implies inactivity; the newly typed inactive conjunctions encode exactly these two cases. No cap rotation invariance or monotonicity of a signed interval term is used. The omitted source only spans `tau ≤ r < kappa`; nonnegative interval-positive and interval-absolute terms make its accepted full tailCost an upper bound for the two halfline tails. Equality r=tau belongs to the tail, and r=kappa is excluded and inactive.

The complete weighted prior prefix proof, lines 1491–1647, was reread with theta and the witness level. Late j>n/160000 and x≥400 imply theta sqrt(j/4)≥1; the support bound gives theta Bcap≤1/100; theta≥0. The actual weighted-strip producer is applied under the reflected prefix law and unchanged beta. The Markov indicator is measurable and L1 by its nonnegative exponentially weighted strip dominator. The new explicit exponential factor equality at 1631–1638 is exactly exp(A−theta L)=exp(A) exp(−theta L), followed by a commutative multiplication rearrangement. It changes no exponent or sign.

The exponent calculation still uses the rational lower square-root bound 88/125, yielding witness payment at least 528x²/125, quadratic cost at most 253x²/125, and hence −11x²/5. The cubic residual pays at most 8 CWRS and support cost at most CWRS/100. The polynomial factor is at most (1+2x)^5. All coefficients and sign conditions were checked in the full proof; the source does not assume an unproved prior payment.

The complete `hBaseDom`, lines 1655–1682, partitions every rank into early/late only after the pointwise comparison. Distributing the outer sum once preserves the paired early summand. In the low-energy branch the finite-rank sum is explicitly converted to the same ordinary Nat-indexed summand; the added late contribution is nonnegative. Equality at the early threshold belongs to earlySet; equality at n/2 belongs to the high branch. This generic deterministic lemma does not assert integrability or independence of M or Hrank.

The complete actual prior domination at 1726–1751 uses the accepted actual prior-hit envelope. `dsimp only at hh` reduces its local let binders without altering the proposition. On the active original strip/witness event, the actual wall is at least the floored wall, so `witnessLevel≤3 actualWall`; the constructed APrior event follows. On its complement the accepted bound is zero, dominated by the nonnegative envelope. The full hLateSum/PriorEnvSum/GPrior block was read: the prefix factor 1/j is bounded by 160000/n only on lateSet, the original W grid sums all true suffix lengths, both walls are integrated using hPairedIntegral, and the factor 6 appears only at actual domination. The total weighted term is `6*320000 CWRS CW delta priorFactor`.

The complete prior payment at 2047–2138 includes its L1 indicators and ordinary fallback. For 16≤x≤400 it uses the positive fixed actual Gaussian tail Psi(400) and ordinary bound; no new C12 fixed-level statement is invoked. For x>400 it uses base plus the integrated full prior envelope. The explicit hIntegralAdd calls have both L1 hypotheses and the correct reordered function. Gaussian absorption of the polynomial and exp(−11x²/5) was read with the full hGaussianLower/PolyTail proof. The coefficient remains `CP=CO/Psi(400)+3(CL+CEarly)+5760000 CWRS CW exp(8CWRS+CWRS/100)+1`.

## Rare suffix, pre-tau and weak-bad payments

The source02 complete proof of the unchanged pre-tau/min-cap/deleted-label block is reused by exact bytes; its current uses and full dependent suffix payments were read in this stage. It uses K=2^64, H=K beta²(1+x)^6, m=ceil(H), tau=min(energyCutoff H,n−m), and lam=min(nu,tau), with the accepted rare producer's p=2 threshold and all its guards. The arbitrary cap need not be invariant under any rotation. The current hBadFuture identification discussed above preserves the m gate and the actual deleted-label energy threshold.

Lines 1826–1909 establish the gated future profile's M/L1/nonnegativity and finite grid payment. The rpow conversion is now explicit: after `rpow_eq_pow`, `rpow_neg` applies because natural t≥0; `sqrt_eq_rpow` converts the denominator, and `one_div` identifies the inverse. This identity is valid also at t=0 with real totalized inverse, while the future payment is used only at m≤t; m≥4 makes that active endpoint positive. For m>t the entire VFuture is zero. Thus no analytic assertion of an actual inverse-square-root singularity at zero is used.

The reverse-grid proof uses the same actual `Fin.rev` value as W. The function provided to hReverseSum is explicitly `t ↦ ∫ u : Path t, VFuture t u ∂law t`, so dependent path dimensions follow the same true suffix length. The harmonic grid includes zero as the zero real reciprocal, and the proof establishes the finite bound ≤2sqrt(n) directly. Its use is multiplied by nonnegative CR Psi(x).

The entire EnvRare/ActualRareDom/RareEnvSum/GRare block, lines 1910–1965, was read. The exact actual strip plus hDRecord plus hBadFuture already closes the active envelope equality; removing subsequent redundant tactics changes no statement. The block lemma provides genuine L1 without conditioning the product law on the pre-tau event. The late sum yields 320000 CU CR delta Psi per wall, then 640000 for both walls through hPairedIntegral. Its factor 6 enters only at the actual weak-bad domination.

The whole final weak-bad comparison and payment, lines 2139–2231, was read, including the local M, T and Hrank values unchanged from source02. Before tau, the two actual rare bounds pay M; after tau, nonnegative full two-wall T pays M. The generic base domination pays low and early ranks before restricting the remaining ranks to lateSet. The explicit Fin/range identity uses the actual closed weak-bad predicate and paired halfline source; it has the same cap and rank. The late tail subset enlarges to all tau-and-later ranks using nonnegativity and is paid by the exact tau..kappa tailCost above.

The final integral uses genuine L1 for bad, base, reordered GRare and tailCost. The new explicit integral function arguments match those four objects. No conditional law, masked independence, hidden residual payment or absolute-value replacement of the full signed bill appears. The total is `3(CL+CEarly)+3840000 CU CR+CT`, absorbed by the unchanged positive `CB` with its extra 1. The proof ends with exactly the ordinary, prior and bad payments required by hPositive.

Unrelated proof bodies in the seven full source files were not claimed as newly reviewed or accepted producer proofs. Required selected heads, necessary complete values and effective ambient were fully read; the output packet records exact source ranges. All 41 mapped targets are mathematical identities, guard manipulations, measurable maps or L1/payment consequences reviewed above. All seven actual diagnostic targets and the necessary new context declarations were inspected. The errors at 1172 and 1391 report `simp made no progress` in the full reverse-suffix-sum and tail finite-sum proofs. These precise failures are preserved, not represented as completed Lean proofs. No implementation edit is made by this reviewer.

The first three failures repeat the same 168 context declarations. The targeted context check reuses 134 exact old declarations and reads all 34 unique newly printed declarations completely, including the new helper, the unchanged accepted omitted-source head with its displayed universe metavariable, and the locally elided data/type declarations. This failure-context reading is not a TYPE/FULLVALUE census: an elided `:= ⋯` is not a full data value, and metavariables/recovery context are not accepted original-object evidence. ## Qualification limits and release

Source03 has failed its first full native gate and has no successful original object to audit. A new immutable repaired version must first pass its own complete native/kernel gate; then all actual-owner TYPE, every actual non-theorem VALUE including auxiliary/local data, and transitive AX must be audited on that same original successful object. The public universe TYPE, actual declaration inventory and dependencies must be verified there. The standard whitelist is only `propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`; no AX evidence for source03 is supplied at this stage. Static absence of forbidden source tokens is not a transitive axiom audit.

No mathematical changes are recommended. There are no critical mathematical gaps found in the reviewed scope. The intended theorem and its current source derivation are mathematically correct; successful Lean encoding and formal acceptance remain unqualified. No root closure follows: this is one full positive/signed separated-overshoot bearing payment, while C2/C12/OQ56 are OPEN, original C1 immutablev85 remains complete, and OQ3 remains separately paused.

The prescribed role is gpt-6.1-sol/xhigh. Actual backend/effort telemetry and input, cached-input, output and reasoning-subset counts are unavailable and recorded as null, separately. No subscription-percentage allocation is inferred. On sealing, this stage has zero writers, executions, inflight calls, pending external actions and children. Root reports the native003 command naturally ended in phase26 and the same author activated for local source04 repair; this reviewer has no server process-observation authority and does not infer any later pass. The next dependency is the new immutable source04's complete affected-proof/data review and exact-source successful native/original-object audits. This release is a bounded completed review stage, not evidence of persistent runtime after the turn ends.
